title: the flags are copied into suffix space the item was never allocated, overwriting the value
live_proof: absent at the pin: 1.6.45:items.c:330-332 carries the fix's guard verbatim -- 'if (nsuffix > 0) { memcpy(ITEM_suffix(it), &flags, sizeof(flags)); }'. A fix-reversal.
object: an item's suffix field, which has NO room of its own when nsuffix is 0
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the item is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: four bytes written into an item field that has no room, inside the chunk
allocator_layer: slabs.c chunks over 1 MiB pages, memcached 1.6.45
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator. The item is laid out in a real slab chunk with nsuffix = 0, where ITEM_suffix and ITEM_data are the SAME address -- asserted by the case -- and nbytes = 2, a zero-length value. A sentinel sits in the two bytes past the value.
distinguishing: a SUB-OBJECT crossing: it overruns the value's storage and stays INSIDE the chunk, so a chunk-granular bound cannot see it. The same shape FFmpeg's subobject-repros corpus is built around, arrived at from the other end. MEASURED only natively. The chunk bound is what the slab port narrows (leases.c carves each chunk), so whether a Capstone arm faults depends on whether this crossing leaves the CHUNK or stays inside it -- stated per case below and NOT measured here: the domain arms need a build this run did not make.
